why: ultra- 'extremely' overlaps mega- 'huge/extremely' (megastar = extremely famous; 'mega rich')
mega- overlaps ultra- 'extremely' in everyday use
civ (Latin civis/civitas) is the source of English 'city'; could be taken as a correct answer for 'city'
hydr 'water' is too close to 'sea' for a learner; ambiguous distractor
quarrelsome means tending to quarrel, not 'tending to cause'; new def covers all four example words (troublesome, tiresome, bothersome = causing; quarrelsome = tending to)
-ous 'full of; having the quality of' overlaps -some (troublesome = full of trouble)
Latin spiritus also means spirit/soul (spirit is a listed word), so 'mind, soul' is defensible for spir
ante- 'before' overlaps 'back in time'; de- 'reverse' overlaps 'backward'
